Signs of the World

Flammable

History

Warnings once read "inflammable", a word easily mistaken to mean something that won't burn, and since the 1950s "flammable" has taken its place. The flame symbol now appears in a red diamond in the Globally Harmonized System for chemical labeling and in a yellow triangle in the ISO 7010 safety standard.

Adoption

A flame over a flat line is read as a fire risk almost anywhere. The diamond is found on chemical containers, while the triangle marks places where fire is a hazard.
